top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is one nameable invention: magic-wavelength trapping cancels the light shift on the clock transition while Lamb-Dicke confinement suppresses Doppler and recoil effects, which lets many neutral atoms be interrogated at once. Katori conceived and first realised it with strontium and Ye brought it to the 1e-18 uncertainty frontier, so the two-person allocation is separable and defensible. Agreement between different species and institutions confirms the uncertainty budgets. The 2005 and 2012 prizes cover the comb and single-ion routes, not the lattice architecture, and no award would waste a mature, well-attributed achievement.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I have no documented connection to Katori or Ye, though as an atomic theorist I know the field and have worked with groups in the attosecond community.
